kitStops: Dubrovnik: A historic walled city on the Adriatic, nicknamed the Pearl of the Adriatic and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. | Walk the City Walls around the old city. | Step through the Pile Gate into the historic centre. | See Big Onofrio's Fountain and the Bell Tower.
Slano: A village in southern Croatia with a small harbour in the bay of the same name.
Korcula: A Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea, known for Grk wine.
Bisevo: A Croatian island in the Adriatic Sea.
Hvar: A Dalmatian town with imposing fortifications and one of the largest squares in Dalmatia. | Visit Humac and the Grapčeva cave.
Stari Grad: A town on Hvar wrapped in the same beautiful Dalmatian coast of stone streets and blue sea. | Explore Humac and the Grapčeva cave.

Split: A city in Central Dalmatia built around the Diocletian palace. | Explore the Basement halls of Diocletian's Palace. | See the Peristylium and St. Duje's cathedral. | Climb St. Duje's bell tower.
Trogir: A medieval town near Split, a popular day trip within its metropolitan area. | Visit St. Lawrence Church. | Explore Kaštel Kamerlengo.

Sibenik: A coastal town with churches, palaces and fortresses to explore. | Visit the Church of Saint Barbara. | See St. Michael's fortress. | Wander the Medieval garden of the monastery St. Laurence.

Vodice: A coastal spot near Sibenik with gardens, churches and fortresses nearby. | See the Church and monastery of St. Francis. | Stroll the Park of Roberto de Visiani. | Visit the Fortress of St. Michael.
Zagreb: The capital of Croatia, with a charming medieval old city. | Visit Zagreb Cathedral. | See St. Mark's Square and Old Town Gate. | Climb Lotrščak Tower.
